items.readable_text:
Content:
Sometimes, a function might increase or decrease without bound when its input gets close to a specific value.

Content:
For example, consider the function whose graph is shown below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/98da7968846584706c506ffa90ca51bf]

Content:
As the input [MATH: x] gets closer to [MATH: 1,] the values of the function get larger and larger.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/a146be634e4b6d7dafe1edfd2515fb4f]

Content:
When this happens, we say that the function approaches "infinity", or that it has an infinite limit at [MATH: x=1.] We can write this mathematically, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: f(x) \rightarrow \infty\quad \text{as}\quad x \rightarrow 1]

Content:
In words, this reads "the function [MATH: f(x)] approaches infinity as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1]".

Content:
Now, consider the function [MATH: y = g(x),] shown below. This is an example of a function that decreases without bound.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d6535b29db21244054364594569cfe1a]

Content:
The function [MATH: g(x)] approaches negative infinity as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1.] So, we can write

Content:
[MATH: g(x) \rightarrow -\infty\quad \text{as } \quad x \rightarrow 1.]

Content:
In words, this reads "the function [MATH: g(x)] approaches negative infinity as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1]".

sections.normalized_html:

  • [MATH: g(x)\rightarrow -\infty] as [MATH: x\rightarrow a]

  • [MATH: g(x)\rightarrow \infty] as [MATH: x\rightarrow b]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/7dfe69669e2d24744e13d0b432fdd7f4]

The graph of the function [MATH: g(x)] is shown above. Find the value of [MATH: b-a,] given the following:

- [MATH: g(x)\rightarrow -\infty] as [MATH: x\rightarrow a]
- [MATH: g(x)\rightarrow \infty] as [MATH: x\rightarrow b]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
From the given graph, we see that as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: -1,] the values of [MATH: g(x)] decrease, approaching [MATH: -\infty.]

So, we can write [MATH: g(x) \to -\infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \to -1.]

Therefore, [MATH: a = -1.]

From the given graph, we see that as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1,] the values of [MATH: g(x)] increase, approaching [MATH: \infty.]

So, we can write [MATH: g(x) \to \infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \to 1.]

Therefore, [MATH: b =1.]

Finally,

[MATH: b - a = 1 - (-1) = 2.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Sometimes, a function might increase or decrease without bound when its input gets close to a specific value.

Content:
For example, consider the function whose graph is shown below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/98da7968846584706c506ffa90ca51bf]

Content:
As the input [MATH: x] gets closer to [MATH: 1,] the values of the function get larger and larger.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/a146be634e4b6d7dafe1edfd2515fb4f]

Content:
When this happens, we say that the function approaches "infinity", or that it has an infinite limit at [MATH: x=1.] We can write this mathematically, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: f(x) \rightarrow \infty\quad \text{as}\quad x \rightarrow 1]

Content:
In words, this reads "the function [MATH: f(x)] approaches infinity as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1]".

Content:
Now, consider the function [MATH: y = g(x),] shown below. This is an example of a function that decreases without bound.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d6535b29db21244054364594569cfe1a]

Content:
The function [MATH: g(x)] approaches negative infinity as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1.] So, we can write

Content:
[MATH: g(x) \rightarrow -\infty\quad \text{as } \quad x \rightarrow 1.]

Content:
In words, this reads "the function [MATH: g(x)] approaches negative infinity as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1]".

---

Item 2 — Example: Identifying Points Where a Function Approaches Infinity

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/7dfe69669e2d24744e13d0b432fdd7f4]

The graph of the function [MATH: g(x)] is shown above. Find the value of [MATH: b-a,] given the following:

- [MATH: g(x)\rightarrow -\infty] as [MATH: x\rightarrow a]
- [MATH: g(x)\rightarrow \infty] as [MATH: x\rightarrow b]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
From the given graph, we see that as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: -1,] the values of [MATH: g(x)] decrease, approaching [MATH: -\infty.]

[IMG: /graphics/3e8287ca47003c02859cc66595347c31]

So, we can write
[MATH: g(x) \to -\infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \to -1.]

Therefore, [MATH: a = -1.]

From the given graph, we see that as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1,] the values of [MATH: g(x)] increase, approaching [MATH: \infty.]

[IMG: /graphics/b53bc2b6d94be347d70c2a3222e4c4b5]

So, we can write
[MATH: g(x) \to \infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \to 1.]

Therefore, [MATH: b =1.]

Finally,

[MATH: b - a = 1 - (-1) = 2.]

---

Item 8 — Tutorial: One-Sided Infinite Behavior of Functions

Content:
We know that some functions approach infinity as [MATH: x] approaches a certain value, like the function [MATH: y=f(x)] plotted below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/ca879394a30973961ecb4f8546f48272]

Content:
Here, the function shoots upwards when [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 2] from the right, that is, from the positive direction of the [MATH: x]-axis.

Content:
We say that the function approaches positive infinity as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 2] from the right, and we write

Content:
[MATH: f(x) \rightarrow \infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \rightarrow 2^+,]

Content:
where the superscript [MATH: +] next to the [MATH: 2] indicates that [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 2] from the right.

Content:
Similar to the case above, we can have a function that shoots upwards or downwards when [MATH: x] approaches a finite value from the left, that is, from the negative direction of the [MATH: x]-axis. Consider the function [MATH: y=g(x),] shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fe3e9e533238ce5840455a36d6091608]

Content:
We say that the function approaches negative infinity as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 2] from the left, and we write

Content:
[MATH: g(x) \rightarrow -\infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \rightarrow 2^-,]

Content:
where the superscript [MATH: -] indicates that [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 2] from the left.

---

Item 9 — Example: Recognizing One-Sided Infinite Behavior of a Function

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/42af81f5a7ff0dd225fbc40f3a0ea1ba]

1. [MATH: f(x) \rightarrow -2]
2. [MATH: f(x)\rightarrow -\infty]
3. [MATH: f(x)\rightarrow \infty]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The notation [MATH: x\rightarrow 1^{+}] means that [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1] from the right.

[IMG: /graphics/8a0f1e5e6a550c7bf86755698132cb82]

From the given graph, we see that as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1] from the right, the values of [MATH: f(x)] increase, approaching [MATH: \infty.]

Therefore, [MATH: f(x)\rightarrow \infty] as [MATH: x \rightarrow 1^{+}.]

Item 12 — Tutorial: Vertical Asymptotes of Functions

Content:
We know that some functions approach infinity as [MATH: x] approaches a certain value from one side, like the functions [MATH: y=f(x)] and [MATH: y=g(x)] plotted below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d7cb0f3f72ad0040b9f076cefa81be10]

Content:
We call the line [MATH: x=2] a vertical asymptote of the functions [MATH: y = f(x)] and [MATH: y=g(x).]

Content:
An asymptote is a line that a function gets very close to but never touches. In general, if a function [MATH: f(x)] has an infinite limit (positive or negative) at a point [MATH: a,] then we write

Content:
[MATH: f(x) \rightarrow \pm \infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \rightarrow a^+]

Content:
or

Content:
[MATH: f(x)\rightarrow \pm\infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \rightarrow a^-]

Content:
and [MATH: x=a] is a vertical asymptote of the function.

---

Explanation:

[IMG: /graphics/bd833c2466e0a3080af61e1f75065d81]

From the given graph, we see that as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: -1] from the left, the values of [MATH: f(x)] increase, approaching [MATH: \infty.] Also, notice that as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: -1] from the right, the values of [MATH: f(x)] decrease, approaching [MATH: -\infty.]

So, we can write:

- [MATH: f(x) \to \infty] as [MATH: x \to -1^-]
- [MATH: f(x) \to -\infty] as [MATH: x \to -1^+]

These give us the same asymptote [MATH: x = -1.]
